- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 10-day average is > 10% above 30-day average, adjust forecast downward by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.5), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 1.0) and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days, then taper to 0% after 7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is > 10% above 30-day moving average, model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven rebound.
